question: Th prime numbers lying between 430 and 443, both included, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the odd numbers between 430 and 443 by eliminating multiples of 3, 5, and divisibility by primes up to 19.

Odd numbers: 431, 433, 435, 437, 439, 441, 443.

Eliminate 435 (ends in 5), 441 (sum of digits is 9 → div by 3), and 437 (19 × 23).

The remaining 4 numbers (431, 433, 439, 443) are not divisible by any prime ≤ 19, hence they are prime.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Range of numbers: 430 to 443 (both included).

**Method Used:**

To check if a number N is prime, we test its divisibility by all prime numbers less than or equal to √N.

For N ≈ 443, √443 ≈ 21.04. So, we test divisibility by primes: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, and 19.

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, eliminate all even numbers (divisible by 2): 430, 432, 434, 436, 438, 440, 442.

⇒ Now, list the remaining odd numbers: 431, 433, 435, 437, 439, 441, 443.

⇒ Eliminate numbers ending in 5 (divisible by 5): 435.

⇒ Eliminate numbers where the sum of digits is divisible by 3: 441 (4 + 4 + 1 = 9).

⇒ Test the remaining numbers (431, 433, 437, 439, 443) for divisibility by 7, 11, 13, 17, and 19.

⇒ 431: Not divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17, or 19. (Prime)

⇒ 433: Not divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17, or 19. (Prime)

⇒ 437: Divisible by 19 (19 × 23 = 437). (Composite)

⇒ 439: Not divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17, or 19. (Prime)

⇒ 443: Not divisible by 7, 11, 13, 17, or 19. (Prime)

⇒ The prime numbers are 431, 433, 439, and 443.

⇒ Total count of prime numbers = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Number Property

A number N > 1 is prime if it is not divisible by any prime number less than or equal to √N.

Twin Primes

Two prime numbers whose difference is exactly 2 are called twin primes. For example, (431, 433) form a twin prime pair.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime (or mutually prime) if their highest common factor (HCF) is 1. They do not necessarily have to be prime individually.
